SECTION ONE
Purpose, Scope, Basis, and Definitions
Purpose
ARTICLE 1- The purpose of this Directive is to determine the general principles and policies regarding the
establishment, dissemination, development , and monitoring of the "Waste Management System", which
aims to protect the environment and human health and all resources in line with the principles of sustainable
development in the processes of collecting, sorting, recycling and disposal of the waste generated as a result
of education, teaching , research, production , and service activities in Gebze Technical University’s (GTU)
divisions.
Scope
ARTICLE 2- This Directive covers all processes from the generation to the recycling of the waste produced
as a result o f use or consumption in GTU’s divisions , including the determination and measurement of the
amount of the recycled waste and its disposal and also the provisions regarding the duties, authorities,
responsibilities, and working procedures of the commission and personnel assigned within this scope.
Basis
ARTICLE 3- This Directive has been prepared based on the "Waste Management Regulation" , which
entered into force after being published in the Official Gazette dated 02/04/2015 and numbered 29314, the
"Zero Waste Regulation" prepared by the Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change of the
Republic of Türkiye, which entered into force after being published in the Official Gazette dated 12/07/2019
and numbered 30829, and the Waste Management Regulation, which entered into force after being
published in the Official Gazette numbered 29314.
Definitions
ARTICLE 4- In this Directive, the following terms have the following definitions:
a) Waste: Wastes generated in GTU's education, teaching, production, service divisions and research
laboratories that cannot be consumed through use or are no longer usable (such as plastic, paper, packaging,
glass, metal, and hazardous waste) as well as all types of materials expected to be released into nature as a
result of use or consumption
b) Divisional Waste Supervisor: Supervisors assigned at GTU's administrative and academic divisions to
carry out the duties specified in this Directive
c) Waste Commission: Zero Waste Commission established within GTU ’s administrative and academic
divisions in order to carry out the duties specified in this Directive
d) Waste Generators: Staff working in GTU’s divisions for education, teaching, research, production, and
service activities; st udents; individuals working in University’s divisions on behalf of contractors; and
visitors to the University
e) Ministry: Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change of the Republic of Türkiye
e) Divisional Waste Plan: Waste plan prepared by the divisional waste supervisors
f) Environmental Management Division Head: GTU Environmental Management Division Head
g)Environmental Management Division Supervisor : GTU Environmental Management Division
Supervisor
h) Rector: GTU Rector
i) Senate: GTU Senate

SECTION TWO
General Principles
General Policies
ARTICLE 5 - (1) To ensure the implementation at the University of the provisions of the Environment Law
No. 2872 dated 09/08/1983, the Waste Management Regulation published in the Official Gazette numbered
29314, and the Zero Waste Regulation published in the Official Gazette dated 12.07.2019 and numbered
30829
(2) To ensure the taking of the highest level of preventive measures to avoid waste generation in University
units unless absolutely necessary
(3) To ensure t hat the waste generated at the University is, if possible, transformed into reusable products,
the amount of recycled waste is measured, and that non-recyclable waste is stored, transported, and disposed
of in a manner that minimizes harmful effects on human health and the environment
(4) To ensure that University staff, students, and on -campus stakeholders are aware of environmental and
waste management in their lives both within and outside the University and to provide training on these
topics
(5) To designate waste supervisors in the University’s divisions and define their responsibilities
(6) To minimize the use of disposable products (plastic, paper, packaging, etc.) and waste within the
University and its supply chain (outsourced)
SECTION THREE
Duties, Authorities, and Responsibilities
Objective of the Waste Commission
Article 6 - To implement the " Waste Management System" to be established within GTU, to ensure
cooperation and coordination with the University’s administration
Governing Bodies of the Waste Commission
Article 7- The bodies of the Waste Commission are as follows:
a) Environmental Management Division Head
b) Waste Commission Members
c) Divisional Waste Supervisors
Designation of Environmental Management Division Head
Article 8- (1) Environmental Management Division Head is assigned by the Rector from among the faculty
members of the University.
(2) The term of office of the Head ends with the appointment of a new head or upon resignation.
Duties, Authorities, and Responsibilities of the Head
Duties, Authorities, and Responsibilities of the Head
Article 9 – The duties, authorities, and responsibilities of the Head are as follows:

a) To execute the programs and activities of the Waste Commission in accordance with the directive and the
decisions of the commission
b) To organize the meetings of the Waste Commission
c) To inform the Rector and the relevant Vice-Rector about the commission's activities
d) To carry out the duties assigned by the Rector or the Vice-Rector assigned by the Rector regarding
matters related to the Waste Management System
e) To implement the decisions of the Waste Commission on waste management
f) To ensure the necessary coordination among the Ministry, Kocaeli Provincial Directorate of Environment,
Urbanization and Climate Change, other public institutions and organizations, and the private sector
g) To organize internal informative and awareness-raising trainings
h) To ensure that the waste is delivered to waste collection and recycling facilities either within or outside
the institution and, if possible, converted into reusable products
i) To perform the other duties assigned by the Rector and the assigned Vice-Rector.
Duties, Authorities, and Responsibilities of the Environmental Management Division Supervisor
Article 10 – The duties, authorities, and responsibilities of the Environmental Management Division
Supervisor are as follows:
a) To fulfill the duties and responsibilities assigned by the Environmental Management Division Head
b) To act as a deputy for the Head in their absence and ensure the continuity of operations
Designation of Divisional Waste Supervisors
Article 11 – Divisional Waste Supervisors are selected from among the members of the University’s
academic and administrative divisions who are assigned by the Rectorate to work in collaboration with the
Waste Commission.
Duties of Divisional Waste Supervisors
Article 12 – The duties of the Divisional Waste Supervisors are as follows:
a) To functionally implement the Waste Directive within their division
b) To prepare divisional waste management plans
c) To determine the needs related to waste management in the division and ensure that these needs are met
d) To keep the waste records submitted by the relevant division supervisors and regularly communicate this
information to the GTU Environment Division
e) To identify, monitor, and take action to reduce activities within the division that have the potential to
generate waste
f) To work towards minimizing single-use product waste (such as plastic, paper, packaging, etc.) on campus
g) To ensure the proper packaging and labeling of wastes to minimize or eliminate their harmful effects on
human health and the environment and to take or ensure the implementation of necessary measures to
minimize waste production
h) To temporarily store or hold the wastes generated within the division in a space allocated by the
division’s senior manager in accordance with the provisions of this Directive, and to ensure their regular

transfer to the waste collection tanks designated by the Rectorate, keeping records of these activities
i) To announce the decisions related to waste management outlined in the Directive, including waste
collection dates, to division staff, students, and other relevant parties
j) To provide information and organize training sessions at regular intervals for division staff and students to
instill awareness for waste management within the University
k) To implement the decisions of the University Waste Management Board and provide full support during
the inspections conducted by the Waste Commission within the division
Formation of the Waste Commission
Article 13 – The Waste Commission consists of members selected from among the Divisional Waste
Supervisors of the University’s academic and administrative divisions, assigned by the Rectorate. The Waste
Commission is responsible for carrying out the duties specified in this Directive.
Duties, Authorities, and Responsibilities of the Waste Commission
Article 14 – The University Waste Commission is a unit under the Rectorate that coordinates all processes
related to the implementation of the University’s Waste Management System and its responsibilities are as
follows:
a) To ensure the implementation at the University of the provisions of the Environment Law No. 2872 dated
09/08/1983, the Waste Regulation, which entered into force after being published in the Official Gazette
numbered 29314, and the Zero Waste Regulation, which entered into force after being published in the
Official Gazette dated 12/07/2019 and numbered 30289, the execution of this Directive and identifying,
offering and applying of solutions for the problems encountered during its execution and to ensure the
implementation of this Directive
b) To follow the current legislation covered under this Directive,
c) To approve the University Waste Management Plan, ensure that the divisions prepare their own waste
management plans, monitor the implementation and updating of these plans at the University
d) To organize trainings and informative meeting on waste management within the divisions
Duties, Authorities, and Responsibilities of Waste Generators
Article 15 – The duties, authorities, and responsibilities of the Waste Generators are as follows:
a) To comply with the practices and principles established in this Directive
b) To adhere to and implement the instructions of the relevant Waste Commission and division supervisors
c) To take the necessary measures to prevent the generation of waste; if prevention is not possible, to
minimize waste production and ensure the reduction or prevention of single-use product waste (such as
plastic, paper, packaging, etc.)
d) To dispose of waste in the collection, storage, and disposal tanks located within GTU based on the waste
content with the purpose of recovering it and reducing/eliminating hazardous content
e) To use products in daily and professional life that are least harmful to the environment after use
f) To be mindful of not carelessly disposing of waste into the environment, to stay informed about
developments regarding waste prevention, and to share thoughts and suggestions with the Divisional Waste
Supervisor

Miscellaneous and Final Provisions
Cases Without Provision
Article 16 – In cases not covered by this Directive, the Senate decision and the relevant legislative
provisions shall apply
Repealed Legislation
Article 17 – As of the date this Directive enters into force, the “Zero Waste Directive” dated 27/08/2020 and
numbered 2020/17-02 has been repealed.
Enforcement
Article 18 – This Directive enters into force on the date it is approved by the GTU Senate.
Execution
Article 19 – The provisions of this Directive are executed by the Rector.
